name: Ed Policy

views.text: A late-season skid does not undo years of good work; we extend the people who built this.
My general manager brings me the big trades; I support him and stay informed.
A rare player is worth the price when the opportunity comes.
We answer to our shareholders and our town, not to a single owner's whims.
Drafting and developing is still the Packers way.
Contending every year is the expectation in Green Bay.

signatures: speaks for a publicly owned club rather than an owner
want: Keep the publicly owned Packers a perennial contender under his presidency (medium).
fear: Being the president when the Packers' long run of stability ends (medium).
voice: Lawyerly, measured and institutional. Speaks for the club and its shareholders, credits his football leaders and avoids personal flourishes.

evidence.summary: Policy announced extensions for coach Matt LaFleur, GM Brian Gutekunst and executive VP Russ Ball despite the season ending with five straight losses.
Green Bay traded two first-round picks and Kenny Clark for Micah Parsons and gave him a four-year, $188 million extension.
Reports Policy was supportive and kept informed of the Parsons pursuit but was not the one who drove it.

review.notes: Thin coverage: two to four sources found by web search (2026-11-06); sliders mostly left at 5; a few publication dates are taken from the news cycle the article covers. Draft for JR to check. Green Bay is publicly owned; this is the team president (Ed Policy, president and CEO from July 2025), not an owner.
